title: Pilot Retrospective: Operations Recommendations & Communication Plan
body:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the post-pilot retrospective for Customer X (3-week pilot), distills operational lessons, and proposes a pragmatic deployment + communications plan for moving from pilot to production (Dedicated or Private). Goal is to present a single-page recommendation for the customer execs and an actionable ops checklist for SRE/SE teams.

Quick verdict (TL;DR):
- Pilot met functional goals: model accuracy within acceptance band for target prompts, 95th percentile latency under 400ms for single-shard requests.
- Production risk is moderate because of burst capacity behavior, KV-cache warmup, and multi-tenant fallback policy gaps.
- Recommended path: staged Dedicated deployment (reserved pool) + small Private gateway for PII-sensitive routes. Priority actions: pin model variant, implement targeted caching policy, and finalize SLA + rollback cadence.

What we ran (short):
- Duration: 3 weeks (2026-02-02 -> 2026-02-23)
- Workloads: interactive chat, document summarization jobs (batch), and embeddings for search reranking.
- Model variants: open-llama-70b-q4 + quantized 4-bit accelerated path for chat; opt-2.7b for embeddings.
- Topology: hosted-hosted baseline then single Dedicated shard on g5x16 during week 3.

Key outcomes and metrics observed:
- Functional: passed acceptance prompts at 92% success (customer threshold 90%).
- Latency: median 120ms (hosted), p95 380ms on Dedicated during concurrent 40 qps spike.
- Throughput: Dedicated shard sustained 250 tokens/sec steady-state on observed prompt mix.
- Cost: estimated hosted token unit cost x1.9 vs Dedicated amortized across reserved capacity; projected 40% cost savings at steady 45 qps with Dedicated.
- Failures: 7 incidents of transient OOM on long-chat sessions (tokens>8k) — root cause: KV cache eviction + mixed quantization kernels.

Root cause summary (ops-focused):
1) KV cache warmup — cold-start on long sessions caused repeated recomputation for early requests. Prefix caching reduces tokens but not sufficient for dynamic docs.
2) Kernel mismatch in mixed-precision path — some model shards used fallback float kernels under memory pressure, creating OOM cascades.
3) Autoscale lag — autoscaler mis-tuned for sudden concurrent bursts (40->80 qps), causing p95 spikes until new nodes registered.
4) Fallback policy gap — when Dedicated pool saturated, routing dropped to incompatible hosted variant (behavior acceptable functionally but unacceptable for latency-sensitive routes).

Recommendations (priority order):
- Immediate (0–2 weeks):
  * Pin the production model variant to the quantized variant we validated. Avoid auto-switching during first 90 days. Owner: SE (Riya) + Product Ops.
  * Deploy targeted KV prefix caching for long-session endpoints; add a small warmup sequence when a new session is opened to pre-populate cache. Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (Diego).
  * Add an emergency quota circuit to throttle extremely long chats rather than let them OOM the cluster. Temporary safeguard for first month. Owner: SRE (Liam).
- Near term (2–8 weeks):
  * Tune autoscaler: reduce registration lag, set proactive scale thresholds for 99th percentile observed burst patterns. Run canary tests (Jenkins pipeline SE-879). Owner: Infra (Samira).
  * Implement graceful fallback policy: route to a lower-latency compatible variant (same tokenization & similar prompt behavior) rather than generic hosted fallback. Work with model catalog. Owner: Product-hosted-api + Serving runtime.
  * Run load test with mixed workloads (chat + batches + embeddings) to validate p95 targets at 2x expected traffic. Test ticket: LOAD-432.
- Medium term (8–16 weeks):
  * Dedicated pool sizing + committed capacity plan with customer finance. Provide 3 sizing options (base/peak/throughput) and cost model. SE to present.
  * Private gateway pilot for PII routes: provide a lightweight VPC bridge and audit logging; target 2-week uplift to deploy. Owner: Private-deployments.

Operational runbook (short checklist):
- Pre-deployment:
  1) Create model pin entry in catalog + freeze rolling updates for model-id: cx-2026-chat-v1.
  2) Add alert: KV-cache hit ratio <60% -> escalate to on-call SRE.
  3) Add alert: p95 latency > 500ms for >5min on critical route.
  4) Add a quota protection: session token cap 10k tokens for first 30 days.
- Day-0 production launch:
  1) Launch Dedicated pool with 2x anticipated baseline capacity.
  2) Monitor cost burn and p95 for the first 48 hours; keep on-call engineer dedicated to the customer channel.
  3) Keep fallback disabled for critical routes for 24 hours; allow only in planned windows.
- Rollback triggers:
  * Repro OOM on >3 distinct nodes within 1 hour.
  * p95 > 700ms for 15 continuous minutes.
  * Unexplained error rate increase >2% of requests.

Communication plan (for customer execs + stakeholders):
- One-pager to customer execs by EOD + 48-hour decision request. Contents: (1) summary of pilot outcome, (2) recommended slot (Dedicated + Private gateway), (3) cost delta and timelines, (4) ask: commit to reserved capacity or start a 90-day evaluation. Owner: SE lead (Maya).
- Technical readout to customer engineering within 3 business days. Include logs, incident timeline, and proposed mitigations. Owner: Riya.
- Internal stakeholders: internal sync with Sales and Finance to finalize pricing & SOW before Week 2 of production. Owner: Solutions AE.

Open questions and risks (customer facing & internal):
- Legal/Security: Is the customer comfortable with short-term session token cap for first 30 days? Legal to confirm. Ticket: LEGAL-201.
- Compliance: Audit log retention requirements for Private gateway — 90 days? 365 days? Need customer input.
- Model drift: plan to run weekly evals on a held prompt set; what threshold triggers a rollback vs retrain? Propose 5% drop in accept rate.

Appendix: notable incidents (short):
- Incident 2026-02-18 09:42 PST: OOM on node rdp-17 during long-session with document >12k tokens. Immediate mitigation: session cap introduced; node rebooted; hotfix to memory alloc thresholds deployed.
- Incident 2026-02-21 16:10 PST: Autoscale lag exposed during marketing demo spike; p95 doubled for ~6 min. Root cause: scale-up TTL set to 90s. Change proposed to 25s and proactive threshold at 75% CPU.

Notes to self (informal):
- Customer X is price sensitive but values latency for chat. Recommend showing 3-year TCO for Dedicated vs hosted with sensitivity bands.
- Keep fallback off on 'customer-sensitive' endpoints until trust built.
- SEs: prepare a short script for the customer support team so they can answer 'why did my chat slow' questions during first week.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Maya: Exec one-pager + send EOD 2026-03-10.
- Riya: Technical readout deck with logs + incident timeline by 2026-03-12.
- Diego: KV prefix caching proposal + PR for warmup sequence by 2026-03-24.
- Samira: Autoscaler tuning plan + canary job by 2026-03-31.
- Liam: Temporary quota circuit implementation by 2026-03-17.

If there are questions or pushback from the customer, escalate to Solutions AE and include Legal early for any session caps or data residency asks.

-- end of doc --
